protocol: Record carrier legal entity, carrier/forwarder/insurer role, mode, service, origin/destination and relevant legs. Do not infer jurisdiction from a brand name.

Separate cargo ownership, agency delegation, insurance interest/subrogation where relevant, contractual rights, data-sharing authority and settlement authority. Have the responsible professional validate permitted handling.

Obtain the governing contract/BOL/tariff/policy as applicable from an authorized owner. Store exact source reference, section/page, effective date, retrieval date and version. Public guidance is context, not a substitute for the applicable agreement.
Separate notice, formal claim, supporting-document requirements and other actions. Identify the triggering event and any exception requiring professional review.
Name the rule owner and reviewer. Record applicability assumptions, source conflict and version conflict. Where unresolved, store null deadline + Verify status; create an evidence chase task.

Only after applicability is established, record the source-supported event/date and calculation with the relevant calendar/timezone. A second reviewer checks the date and its meaning. Do not generate a universal default.
Display carrier, mode, contract version, source link, trigger, owner, review date and verification status alongside the task. A reminder is not a legal opinion or promise of timeliness.

Version each rule update, flag affected cases for re-verification, retain previous calculation and approvals, and stop stale automations until reviewed. Unknown or contradictory sources remain blocked.

Claimant approves any future submission workflow. Settlement, coverage, legal advice and insurance adjustment stay with properly authorized/licensed parties. The public concept only generates synthetic review/export states.
